title: 木兰花·池塘水绿风微暖
title_en: Magnolia Blossoms: The Pond Is Green, the Breeze a Little Warm
author: 晏殊

text_note.zh: 这里用《宋词三百首》等通行本的文字，作者晏殊，词牌《木兰花》。我们的资料库把它收在欧阳修名下，词牌作《玉楼春》（和《木兰花》是同一个曲调），文字有几处不同：“春微暖”“从头歌韵响铮𫓩”“玉钩帘下”“红日晚”。
text_note.en: This page follows the common text in Three Hundred Song Lyrics and other usual editions, by Yan Shu, under the tune name Magnolia Blossoms. Our source text files it under Ouyang Xiu with the tune name Jade Tower Spring, which is another name for the same tune. Its words differ in a few places: "spring a little warm" instead of "the breeze a little warm", "from the beginning" instead of "the repeated part", a metal-like ringing instead of a jade-like one, "a curtain on jade hooks" instead of "a carved railing", and "the red sun" instead of "the setting sun".

readings.zh: “重头”的“重”是重复的意思，读 chóng，不读 zhòng。
readings.en: Here the character means repeated, so it is read chóng, not zhòng.

readings.zh: “琤琮”读 chēng cóng，是玉石相碰的声音。“琤”这个字很少见。
readings.en: These two characters are read chēng cóng; they are the sound of jade striking jade. The first one is rare.

readings.zh: “乱旋”的“旋”是旋转的意思，读 xuán。
readings.en: Here the character means to spin, so it is read xuán.

glosses.zh: 风微暖：风微微有些暖和。
glosses.en: fēng wēi nuǎn: the breeze is a little warm.

glosses.zh: 玉真：本来指仙女，这里指一位像仙女一样美的歌舞女子。
glosses.en: yù zhēn: a fairy; here it means a singer and dancer as lovely as a fairy.

glosses.zh: 重头：词的上下两段节拍完全一样，叫“重头”。这里指她唱的曲子。
glosses.en: chóng tóu: when the two halves of a song have exactly the same beat, it is called a repeated head. Here it means the song she sang.
gē yùn: the tune of the singing.

glosses.zh: 琤琮：玉石相碰的清脆声音，这里形容歌声清亮。
glosses.en: chēng cóng: the clear sound of jade striking jade; here it describes a bright, clear voice.

glosses.zh: 入破：唐宋大曲里的一段，到这里节奏突然变快，舞蹈也跟着急促起来。
glosses.en: rù pò: a part of a long Tang and Song dance suite where the beat suddenly speeds up and the dance grows fast.

glosses.zh: 舞腰红乱旋：跳舞的人腰身转动，红色的衣裙飞快地旋转。
glosses.en: wǔ yāo hóng luàn xuán: the dancer's waist turns and her red skirt whirls fast.

glosses.zh: 玉钩阑：雕饰精美的栏杆。
glosses.en: yù gōu lán: a finely carved railing.

glosses.zh: 香阶：落着花瓣、带着香气的台阶。
glosses.en: xiāng jiē: steps scented by fallen petals.

glosses.zh: 斜日：西斜的太阳。“斜日晚”是说太阳快落山了。
glosses.en: xié rì: the sun sinking in the west. Xié rì wǎn means the sun is going down.

glosses.zh: 点检：一个一个地清点、数。
glosses.en: diǎn jiǎn: to count one by one.

translation.zh: 池塘里的水绿了，风微微暖和起来。
translation.en: The pond water has turned green, and the breeze is a little warm.

translation.zh: 我还记得第一次见到那位像仙女一样美的姑娘。
translation.en: I still remember the first time I saw that girl, lovely as a fairy.

translation.zh: 她唱着上下两段相同的曲子，歌声像玉石相碰一样清脆。
translation.en: She sang a song whose two halves match, her voice ringing clear like jade on jade.

translation.zh: 舞曲节奏变快，她腰身转动，红裙飞旋。
translation.en: When the music sped up, her waist turned and her red skirt whirled.

translation.zh: 在精美的栏杆下，在花香飘飘的台阶旁，
translation.en: Below the carved railing, beside the petal-scented steps,

translation.zh: 我喝醉了，连太阳快落山了都不知道。
translation.en: I was so drunk I did not notice the sun was going down.

translation.zh: 当年和我一起赏花的那些人，
translation.en: Of the people who enjoyed the flowers with me back then,

translation.zh: 如今数一数，已经不到一半了。
translation.en: if I count them now, not even half are left.

background.zh: 这首词回忆多年前一个春天，在宴会上初见一位歌舞女子的情景，结尾感叹当年一起赏花的人如今已经不到一半。《宋词三百首》等通行选本都把它算作晏殊的《木兰花》；一说是欧阳修写的，欧阳修名下也有这首词，只有几个字不同。写作时间不清楚；一说写于晏殊晚年在永兴军（今陕西西安一带）做官的时候。
background.en: This lyric looks back to a spring many years ago, when the poet first saw a young singer and dancer at a feast. At the end he sighs that, of the friends who enjoyed the flowers with him then, not even half are left. Three Hundred Song Lyrics and other common anthologies count it as Yan Shu's Magnolia Blossoms. Another view says Ouyang Xiu wrote it, and the same lyric, with a few words different, is also filed under his name. We do not know for sure when it was written; one view is that it was when Yan Shu, late in life, held office in Yongxing, near today's Xi'an.

author_note.zh: 晏殊（991—1055），字同叔，抚州临川（今属江西）人，北宋词人，做官做到宰相。他小时候就被称为神童。他的词集叫《珠玉词》，多写宴会、春光和淡淡的感伤。欧阳修年轻时得到他的赏识，两人词风很接近，所以有些词同时出现在两人的集子里，这首就是一例。
author_note.en: Yan Shu (991–1055), courtesy name Tongshu, came from Linchuan in today's Jiangxi. He was a Northern Song lyric poet who rose to chancellor. As a boy he was already called a child prodigy. His collection is called Pearls and Jade Lyrics, and it is mostly about feasts, spring light and a gentle sadness. When Ouyang Xiu was young, Yan Shu valued his talent. Their styles are close, so some lyrics turn up in both men's collections, and this is one of them.

appreciation.zh: 上半首像一段彩色的回忆：春天的池塘绿了，那位姑娘第一次出现。她唱起歌来，声音清脆得像玉石相碰；节奏一快，她的红裙转成一团火。读的时候，好像自己也坐在宴会上，看得入了迷。下半首接着写那天的快乐：栏杆下、台阶前，大家喝得大醉，太阳落山都不知道。最后两句一下子回到现在：当年一起赏花的人，数一数已经不到一半。热闹的过去和冷清的现在放在一起，时光飞逝、人事无常的感慨说得很轻，却让人久久难忘。
appreciation.en: The first half is like a colorful memory. The spring pond is green, and the girl appears for the first time. She sings, her voice as clear as jade striking jade. When the beat speeds up, her red skirt spins like a flame. As you read, it is as if you sit at the feast too, lost in the show. The second half goes on with that happy day: below the railing, by the steps, everyone got so drunk that no one noticed the sunset. Then the last two lines jump back to now. Of the friends who enjoyed the flowers together, not even half are left. Putting the lively past next to the lonely present, the poem says softly how fast time flies and how nothing stays the same, and the feeling stays with you.
